evidence: (a) Equivalent mechanisms found but incomplete: stable seat IDs and template-member correspondence (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:8,25-26; DESIGN-NOTES.md:291-303) identify seats; grouped hydration action records list created/reused IDs for undo (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:26,53-55; DESIGN-NOTES.md:283-286,302). Those records describe a historical action, not the scope of later named-group list/retire/resurrect. (b) The approved tradeoff is no required extra per-seat hydration identity or group node (DESIGN-NOTES.md:300-302; :75), not abandonment of the named collective experience promised at :39. Hydration undo's explicit preserve-reused rule (:286) covers undo, not ordinary group retirement. (c) Collective lifecycle is within stated scope: DESIGN-NOTES.md:39 and HERDR-GRAPH-VISION.md:120; SOFTWARE-FACTORY-VISION.md:64,149 expects a temporary feature group to join and retire. (d) Material ambiguity: if named group A reuses an existing seat, then adds or excludes another seat, its historical hydration record cannot alone determine which seats and threads a later group retirement should affect; treating reused seats as members could retire a responsibility belonging to another group, while ignoring current additions could strand part of the intended group. Current design explicitly leaves repeated composition/correspondence open (CURRENT-DESIGN.md:27; DESIGN-NOTES.md:296). Narrowing: the design need not automatically include every later team addition, nor add a durable group node; it needs an explicit membership/scope rule for collective operations. This is an acknowledged design-stage gap, not evidence of implemented loss. No external premise is used.
